Architecture and rationale

## **Compound explanations and operational synthesis**



226. Compounds, mechanisms, pairings and timing



### **VII Core daily and pulsed compounds**

- **Intranasal insulin**. 20 to 25 IU before or during a study block, with no more than two administrations a day and at least four hours between them. The intended role is to support GluA1 AMPA receptor insertion in the CA1 region and dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, alongside striatal cholinergic and dopaminergic activity, while avoiding desensitization involving Grb10, mTORC1 and IRS-1 Ser636 and Ser639. It is paired with pulsed TAK-653.
- **TAK-653, also called osavampator**. 0.5 to 1.0 mg on Monday, Wednesday and Friday. It is an AMPA receptor positive allosteric modulator, intended to amplify active glutamatergic currents across cortical networks and help link concepts, with minimal desensitization. Rehearse with mock exams before using it for live tests.
- **KW-6356, also called sipagladenant**. 1 to 2.5 mg at 7 am on days 1 and 4. Its intended role is to reduce the perceived cost of effort through striatopallidal A2A inverse agonism without spending dopamine. The twice weekly pulse reflects its reported half life of 18.4 to 43.1 hours and the concern about suppressing nocturnal spindle and ripple coupling. Armodafinil alternates on days 2, 3, 5 and 6. Istradefylline is the shorter acting A2A alternative.
- **Safinamide**. 50 mg daily alongside KW-6356. The proposed role of reversible monoamine oxidase B inhibition is to raise phasic striatal dopamine and limit the conversion of spermidine and putrescine from the height protocol into astrocytic tonic GABA through Best1.
- **Guanfacine**. 0.25 to 1.5 mg every day, either in the evening or 90 minutes beforehand. It acts on postsynaptic alpha 2A receptors in layer III of the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex. The intended effect is to reduce cyclic AMP in dendritic spine necks, keep HCN and KCNQ leak channels closed and preserve working memory under time pressure and stimulant surges.
- **ACD856**. 3 to 10 mg between 2 pm and 2.30 pm, or 120 minutes before the end of the study block. It is a positive allosteric modulator of Trk receptors, timed so its two hour peak coincides with the late study block rise in BDNF. The proposed effect is to favor Hrs dependent endosomal recycling of TrkB over lysosomal degradation. It is paired with cilostazol.
- **Cilostazol**. 25 mg at 4.30 pm. Through PDE3 inhibition, it is intended to support CREB dependent capture of synaptic tags and microvascular perfusion after the ACD856 learning window.
- **Daridorexant**. 25 mg at 11 pm. It blocks both orexin receptors to reduce nighttime arousal, supporting low acetylcholine slow wave sleep, sharp wave ripple replay and the nocturnal growth hormone pulse. Vornorexant at 10 to 20 mg is listed as the shorter acting alternative. Fasted doxepin at 1 to 3 mg is the H1 alternative for the final third of sleep.



### **VIII Conceptualization and broader understanding**

- **522-054**. 50 to 200 mcg, 30 minutes beforehand. It combines positive modulation of alpha 7 nicotinic receptors with negative modulation of alpha 5 GABA A receptors, with the aim of making relevant cues stand out on the first read.
- **TAK-071**. Conditional. It is a low cooperativity positive allosteric modulator of M1 muscarinic receptors, intended to sharpen cortical cue discrimination without peripheral cholinergic gastrointestinal side effects. AVL-3288 is the type I alpha 7 positive modulator alternative, while basmisanil is the selective alpha 5 GABA A negative modulator alternative.
- **Coluracetam**. 10 to 20 mg in the morning. It enhances high affinity choline uptake to support acetylcholine synthesis during dense analytical reading. It is paired with tropisetron at 2.5 to 5 mg as the accessible alpha 7 nicotinic receptor partner.
- **Phenylpiracetam hydrazide**. 50 to 100 mg in the morning, at most twice a week on test or showcase days. Its intended role is a fast AMPA potent state for higher order execution during demanding problem solving.
- **Nefiracetam**. 50 to 100 mg 60 minutes beforehand, only on days when TAK-653 is off. It is intended to disinhibit PKC and CaMKII signaling and preserve synaptic plasticity under heavy stress.
- **AF710B**. 10 to 25 mg 60 minutes beforehand. It combines M1 muscarinic and sigma 1 chaperone activation to stabilize calcium transfer between the endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria under high cognitive load. Pridopidine at 22.5 to 45 mg is the dedicated sigma 1 chaperone alternative for their contact sites.
- **ASP4345**. In the morning or 60 minutes beforehand. It is a selective dopamine D1 positive allosteric modulator, intended to stabilize multistep derivations in prefrontal working memory without the usual stimulant load.
- **Cerebrolysin**. 5 to 10 mL intramuscularly in periodic cycles of five days on and two days off. Its role here is broader neurotrophic peptide support once energy and choline needs are met.
- **5-MeO-DMT**. 2 to 5 mg in a separate session outside study. Its intended role is an acute network reset and change in perspective, kept strictly separate from analytical study blocks.



### **IX ΓÇâ INFORMATION RETENTION AND MEMORY**

- **Edonerpic maleate**. Immediately after verified learning sessions. It binds CRMP2 and is intended to drive activity dependent movement of AMPA receptors into newly practiced dendritic spines. It is reserved for after accurate recall so errors are not consolidated.
- **BPN14770, also called zatolmilast**. 1 to 25 mg every other day alongside guanfacine. It selectively inhibits PDE4D allosterically and is intended to increase hippocampal cyclic AMP, PKA and CREB tag capture without the nausea associated with broader PDE4 inhibition. TAK-915 or roflumilast at 50 to 100 mcg are listed as PDE2A and PDE4 alternatives.
- **Usmarapride**. In the morning before encoding, never within eight hours of sleep. It is a partial 5-HT4 agonist intended to increase hippocampal acetylcholine release during encoding and shift APP toward neuroprotective sAPP alpha. Prucalopride at 1 to 2 mg in the morning is the accessible 5-HT4 alternative.
- **Brivaracetam**. 10 to 25 mg 30 to 45 minutes beforehand, replacing levetiracetam. It is a rapidly equilibrating SV2A modulator intended to quiet hippocampal DG and CA3 hyperexcitability so similar facts do not blur together. Hold it on multistep derivation or exam days. Amisulpride at 100 to 200 mg is listed as the D2 and D3 alternative for interference.
- **ISRIB**. 2.5 to 10 mg intranasally, two to three times a week for a maximum of two to three weeks. The limit is eight to ten administrations, followed by a washout of at least two weeks. It activates eIF2B allosterically and is intended to lift the phosphorylated eIF2 alpha translational brake after verified mastery. DNL343 or 2BAct is listed as the clinical eIF2B alternative.
- **Nooglutyl**. 10 to 25 mg 45 minutes beforehand. It is an AMPA and glutamatergic encoding enhancer used when dense new material does not register on the first pass.
- **CDP-choline**. 250 mg in the morning and paired with uridine monophosphate. It supplies choline and cytidine to support acetylcholine and phosphatidylcholine during long study blocks.
- **Uridine monophosphate**. 250 mg in the morning alongside CDP-choline. Its role is to replenish UTP and synaptic membrane phosphatides.



### **X ΓÇâ MOTIVATION, DRIVE AND TASK ENGAGEMENT**

- **BTRX-246040, also called LY2940094**. Daily or around a session. It is a selective nociceptin receptor antagonist paired with KW-6356 to address the nucleus accumbens quitting signal triggered by competing high dopamine distractions.
- **Aticaprant**. Conditional. It blocks kappa opioid receptors and is intended to reduce dynorphin mediated ventral striatal dysphoria and aversive resistance to a task. Navacaprant is the equivalent kappa opioid receptor alternative. Ultra low dose buprenorphine at 0.10 to 0.15 mg sublingually, capped at one to two times a week, is the partial mu and kappa receptor fallback.
- **Low dose amisulpride**. 12.5 to 25 mg in the morning, cycled at most three to four days per week. Its proposed role is to block presynaptic D2 and D3 autoreceptors, releasing endogenous phasic dopamine to support task initiation.
- **Phenylpiracetam**. 100 mg in the morning in cycles. It is used as a dopamine transporter and nicotinic execution driver, rotated with catecholaminergic activity enhancers to limit tolerance.
- **The negative enantiomer of BPAP, or PPAP**. Rotation days. It is a catecholaminergic activity enhancer intended to amplify action potential evoked catecholamine release without carrier mediated depletion of stores. Sublingual selegiline or amantadine are the accessible rotation alternatives.
- **Irdabisant**. 25 to 100 mcg in the morning. It is a potent H3 autoreceptor inverse agonist intended to increase histaminergic and cholinergic wakefulness on days without armodafinil. Pitolisant or the orexin 2 receptor agonist oveporexton, also called TAK-861, are wakefulness alternatives on days without meclizine.
- **Armodafinil**. 50 to 100 mg in the morning on days 2, 3, 5 and 6. It is a low affinity dopamine transporter wakefulness driver, alternated with KW-6356 on days 1 and 4 and cycled with pitolisant.
- **SAMe**. 400 mg a day for methyl donor and catecholamine support. It is paired with MSM at 1,000 to 2,000 mg a day to buffer transsulfuration demand.



### **XI ΓÇâ BRAIN FOG AND COGNITIVE DURABILITY**

- **Creatine monohydrate**. 5,000 to 20,000 mg in the morning, at least four hours apart from taurine. It is the main CK-B phosphocreatine ATP buffer in the protocol, intended to support frequent cortical firing and resilience to sleep debt. It is paired with guanidinoacetic acid and betaine.
- **Guanidinoacetic acid**. 1,000 to 2,000 mg in the morning, at least four hours apart from taurine, alongside betaine at 1,500 mg a day. It crosses the choroid plexus through GAT2 and TauT for methylation into brain creatine by astrocytic GAMT. Cyclocreatine is the low equilibrium constant alternative, intended to continue releasing phosphate during late session acidosis.
- **Terazosin**. 0.5 to 0.8 mg at bedtime and paired with trimetazidine. It allosterically activates PGK1 to support neuronal glycolytic ATP, pyruvate and citrate supply. It is held the night before exams.
- **Extended release trimetazidine**. 15 to 30 mg. It inhibits 3-KAT and fatty acid beta oxidation to shift neuronal mitochondria toward the more oxygen efficient use of glucose. Elamipretide, also called SS-31, with triheptanoin is the alternative aimed at cardiolipin and seven carbon anaplerosis.
- **Enteric coated ethyl pyruvate**. 500 mg, 60 to 75 minutes before NMNH. It provides a cytosolic LDH pyruvate electron sink that oxidizes NADH to oxidized NAD. The aim is to prevent subsequent NAD precursor loading from raising the NADH to oxidized NAD ratio or triggering SARM1 related reductive stress.
- **NMNH, or reduced nicotinamide mononucleotide**. 100 mg, 60 to 75 minutes after enteric coated ethyl pyruvate. Its intended role is to replenish neuronal oxidized NAD after intensive cognitive blocks once the pyruvate electron sink is in place.
- **Myo-inositol and D-chiro-inositol**. Before study or during a session, paired with R-alpha-lipoic acid. They generate inositol phosphoglycan second messengers that activate mitochondrial pyruvate dehydrogenase phosphatase. The intended effect is to sustain acetyl-CoA flux beyond the second hour after surface insulin receptors desensitize.
- **Pinealon**. 0.25 to 0.5 mg subcutaneously in the morning or evening. It is included as a tripeptide for neuronal recovery during high load periods, with an intended anti hypoxic effect.
- **Magnesium acetyl-taurate**. 400 to 600 mg a day alongside L-carnosine at 1,000 mg a day. It is intended to reach the central nervous system and support KCC2 chloride extrusion and magnesium gating of NMDA receptors.
- **Pyrroloquinoline quinone, also called PQQ**. 20 mg twice daily. It is intended to activate PGC-1alpha mitochondrial biogenesis and redox cofactor cycling.
- **L-ergothioneine**. 2 to 5 mg a day. It concentrates in mitochondria through OCTN1 and is intended to scavenge hydroxyl and peroxynitrite radicals under load.
- **Urolithin A**. 250 to 500 mg a day. Its role is to maintain PINK1 and Parkin mitophagy quality control across both the cognition and height protocols.



### **XII Timed exams and late afternoon study**

- **Nicergoline**. 5 to 10 mg 90 minutes before an exam, alongside guanfacine and TAK-653, with terazosin held the night before. It is intended to provide mild alpha 1 adrenergic protection against exam stress related norepinephrine surges and support cerebral perfusion without an orthostatic alpha 1B drop.
- **Immediate release dexmethylphenidate**. 2.5 to 5 mg, 45 minutes before an exam or at 4.30 pm for late afternoon cramming. The listed cutoff is 5 pm, with at least 60 percent of daily calories consumed before 4 pm and vornorexant or daridorexant at 11 pm. The intended dopamine and norepinephrine transporter effect is followed 20 minutes before the exam by 20 to 25 IU of intranasal insulin. Azstarys or S-CE-123 are listed as dopamine transporter alternatives.



### **XIII Frontier options in order of priority**

- **OV350, with OV4071 or AXN-027 as alternatives**. Conditional. It directly activates KCC2 chloride extrusion and is intended to restore the outward chloride gradient when prolonged study weakens GABA A hyperpolarization and competing representations intrude. It is paired with AUT00206.
- **AUT00206, or AUT5**. Conditional. It modulates Kv3.1 and Kv3.2 potassium channels on parvalbumin expressing fast spiking basket cells, with the aim of sharpening gamma synchrony once OV350 has restored the chloride gradient.
- **VU6053371**. Conditional. It is a selective postsynaptic mGlu3 positive allosteric modulator intended to limit spine neck cyclic AMP and HCN leak without a systemic blood pressure drop. 2-MPPA is the alternative route through GCPII and preservation of NAAG.
- **Neboglamine, also called S-CR-2249**. Conditional. It is a positive allosteric modulator at the GluN1 glycine site, intended to widen the NMDA coincidence detection window for synthesis across several variables. The NMDA alternatives are dalzanemdor, also called SAGE-718, a microdose of D-cycloserine, or sarcosine with magnesium L-threonate.
- **YX968**. After mastery. It is a selective HDAC3 and HDAC8 PROTAC degrader intended to enable long term epigenetic memory consolidation without the nuclear ACSS2 depletion associated with broader HDAC inhibition. CSP-TTK21, P10 or P13 are listed as direct alternatives acting on CBP and p300 or Tip60 histone acetyltransferases.
- **Dihexa**. 5 mg intranasally three times a week, strictly after verified mastery. It is an HGF and MET synaptogenic agonist intended to turn practiced synaptic tags into durable mushroom spines. SPG302 is the nonpeptide alternative for spine formation.
- **KDS-2010, with tisolagiline or SMP-100 as alternatives**. Daily. It is a highly selective reversible astrocytic monoamine oxidase B inhibitor intended to stop putrescine derived tonic GABA and hydrogen peroxide related fog without irreversible enzyme inhibition.
- **Senicapoc**. Conditional. It selectively blocks microglial KCa3.1 and is intended to prevent complement mediated synaptic pruning under sleep debt. Ibudilast at 10 to 20 mg or dapansutrile are the accessible glial and NLRP3 alternatives.
- **S107, or ARM210**. Conditional. It stabilizes RyR2 and calstabin2 to close neuronal calcium leak associated with PKA hyperphosphorylation under chronic stress.
- **Evenamide, or extended release ranolazine**. Conditional. It selectively blocks persistent inward sodium current to prevent exhaustion of axonal sodium potassium ATPase during sustained firing. The negative enantiomer of OSU6162 or pirepemat are listed as monoaminergic floor stabilizers.
- **Azetukalner, also called XEN1101**. Conditional evening option. It opens Kv7.2 and Kv7.3 potassium channels to reset cortical hyperexcitability after high gain study blocks.
- **Zagociguat**. Daily. It is a central nervous system penetrating soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator, paired with sepiapterin for BH4 dependent eNOS recoupling to restore neurovascular coupling during long blocks.
- **Elunetirom, also called Sob-AM2**. Daily. It is a FAAH cleaved thyromimetic selective for the central nervous system, intended to support central oligodendrocyte and mitochondrial function without peripheral thyrotoxicosis.
- **2-HOBA**. In the morning only. Its intended role is to scavenge reactive isoketal gamma ketoaldehydes before they crosslink synaptic proteins during high oxidative flux.

# **I. Core Endocrine and Signaling Drivers (Days 1ΓÇô14)**

- **Dabogratinib (TYRA-300)** ΓÇö 0.25 mg/kg/day ΓÇö selective **FGFR3 tyrosine kinase inhibition** in proliferating and pre-hypertrophic chondrocytes that releases the STAT1 and MAPK/ERK brake on proliferation and hypertrophy while sparing FGFR1 phosphate and FGFR4 bile-acid burden (**erdafitinib** is the alternative pan-FGFR1/3 branch that requires the Section II shield).
- **Somatropin (GH)** ΓÇö 12ΓÇô15 IU/day ΓÇö primary **systemic and epiphyseal IGF-1 drive** in open growth plates, bounded by downstream secretory capacity and terminal conversion margin so recruitment does not outrun resting-zone self-renewal.
- **Anastrozole** ΓÇö 0.5ΓÇô1 mg/day ΓÇö non-steroidal **aromatase inhibition** that slows intracrine **ER-alpha resting-zone stem senescence** and preserves the open physeal horizon (**exemestane** 12.5ΓÇô25 mg every 3 days or **Z-endoxifen** 1ΓÇô2 mg/day are mutually exclusive substitutes, never combined).
- **Racecadotril** ΓÇö 100 mg two to three times daily ΓÇö peripheral **ecto-neprilysin (NEP) inhibition** that preserves local **CNP** at the growth plate so NPR2ΓÇôcGMPΓÇôPKGII signaling stays active (**sacubitrilat** is the separate NEP alternative; paired with **cilostazol**).
- **Cilostazol** ΓÇö 25 mg twice daily ΓÇö **PDE3 inhibition** and microvascular **cAMP/NO vasodilation** that supports perichondrial perfusion and cyclic-nucleotide signaling alongside **racecadotril** (distinct from downstream NPR2/BK/TRPM7 execution).
- **Spermidine trihydrochloride** ΓÇö 5 mg/day (\~2.85 mg spermidine) ΓÇö obligate aminobutyl substrate for **deoxyhypusine synthase (DHS)** to hypusinate **eIF5A** when polyproline translation limits Col2a1 and Col10a1 elongation (paired with **brazilin**).
- **Brazilin** ΓÇö daily ΓÇö supports **deoxyhypusine hydroxylase (DOHH)** to complete the second catalytic step of **eIF5A hypusination** initiated by **spermidine**.

## **II. Erdafitinib Targeted Ancillaries (Active When Using Pan-FGFR Inhibition)**

- **Sucroferric oxyhydroxide** ΓÇö meal-linked ΓÇö non-absorbed **luminal phosphate binder** that captures dietary phosphate first under FGFR1 blockade (isolate ΓëÑ3 hours from **copper, manganese, buffered vitamin C, and citrate**; binder release follows recovering phosphate handling rather than a fixed mineralization holiday).
- **Nicotinamide** ΓÇö meal-linked ΓÇö slower intestinal **NaPi-IIb cotransporter restraint** that complements luminal binding by **sucroferric oxyhydroxide** (distinct from **NR** NAD+ salvage; note **dipyridamole** preserves extracellular adenosine but blocks ENT1/2 cellular entry of NR and inosine).
- **Tenapanor** ΓÇö conditional meal-linked ΓÇö intestinal **NHE3 inhibition** that reduces residual paracellular phosphate absorption when meal-linked binding plus **nicotinamide** leave serum phosphate elevated (bounded by GI fluid loss).
- **Rebamipide** ΓÇö 100 mg three times daily ΓÇö **mucosal prostaglandin and epithelial restitution** against FGFR-inhibitor wear (add **irsogladine** only when coordinated epithelial closure lags, weighed against its possible **MMP-13 restraint** at the terminal growth front).
- **Finerenone** ΓÇö conditional ΓÇö non-steroidal **mineralocorticoid receptor antagonism** for the leak-side hypothesis of FGFR/MAPK **subretinal fluid** (**eplerenone** is the steroidal MRA alternative; shares the daily potassium budget with **potassium citrate**).
- **Dorzolamide (topical ophthalmic)** ΓÇö conditional ΓÇö local **carbonic anhydrase II/IV inhibition** for the clearance-side hypothesis of subretinal fluid, selected by retinal findings.
- **Colesevelam** ΓÇö conditional ΓÇö luminal **bile-acid sequestrant** added when FGFR4/FGF19 blockade warrants bile-acid capture (separate ΓëÑ4 hours from **TUDCA, aromatase inhibitors, TKIs, and vitamins D3/K2**).
- **Meclozine** ΓÇö 25ΓÇô50 mg conditional bedtime ΓÇö distal **ERK1/2 attenuation** branch that reduces required pan-FGFR pressure, weighed against next-day sedation opposing cognition.

## **III. Continuous Folding, Bioenergetic and Cofactor Base (Days 1ΓÇô14)**

- **Vitamin D3** ΓÇö 800ΓÇô2,000 IU/day ΓÇö baseline **25(OH)D mineral sufficiency** (held if pan-FGFR inhibition elevates endogenous calcitriol).
- **Vitamin K2 (MK-7)** ΓÇö 100ΓÇô200 mcg/day ΓÇö continuous **baseline GGCX carboxylation** of matrix Gla protein (**MGP**) and osteocalcin.
- **Ubiquinol** ΓÇö 100 mg/day ΓÇö reduced **coenzyme Q10 electron carrier** supporting mitochondrial respiratory coupling and membrane antioxidant protection.
- **Nicotinamide riboside chloride (NR)** ΓÇö 568 mg/day ΓÇö expands the chondrocyte **NAD+ pool** to sustain glycolytic flux and sirtuin deacetylase activity (distinct from nicotinamide NaPi-IIb phosphate transport control).
- **Urolithin A** ΓÇö 250ΓÇô500 mg/day ΓÇö supports **PINK1/Parkin mitophagy** and mitochondrial quality control in resting and proliferating chondrocytes.
- **Ergothioneine** ΓÇö 5 mg/day ΓÇö **OCTN1-transported cytoprotective thiol/thione** that buffers mitochondrial and stromal oxidative stress without scavenging physiological signaling peroxides.
- **Pyridoxamine** ΓÇö 100ΓÇô200 mg/day ΓÇö traps reactive **dicarbonyl Amadori intermediates** before non-enzymatic AGE cross-links stiffen the collagen network (paired with **L-carnosine**).
- **L-carnosine** ΓÇö 500 mg twice daily ΓÇö buffers intracellular glycolytic protons and scavenges **4-HNE and ╬▒,╬▓-unsaturated aldehydes** alongside **pyridoxamine**.
- **Buffered vitamin C** ΓÇö 200 mg/day ΓÇö obligate reducing cofactor that maintains **P4HA1 prolyl-4-hydroxylase** catalytic Fe2+ activity for procollagen triple-helix folding (isolate ΓëÑ3 hours from iron phosphate binders).
- **Copper bisglycinate** ΓÇö 2 mg/day ΓÇö obligate cofactor for **lysyl oxidase (LOX)** interterritorial collagen II cross-linking (isolate ΓëÑ3 hours from iron binders to prevent duodenal DMT1 competition).
- **Manganese bisglycinate** ΓÇö 2 mg/day ΓÇö obligate cofactor for **Golgi XylT and B4GALT7 glycosyltransferases** that initiate chondroitin sulfate chains on aggrecan (isolate ΓëÑ3 hours from iron binders and calcium).

## **IV. Stage 1A and 1B ΓÇö Matrix Synthesis and Swelling Build (Days 1ΓÇô6)**

- **L-glutamine** ΓÇö 5,000 mg twice daily ΓÇö primary nitrogen and carbon donor for the **GFAT1 hexosamine pathway** and ╬▒-ketoglutarate cofactor supply for procollagen hydroxylation.
- **L-proline** ΓÇö 460 mg twice daily (with dietary/supplemental **glycine** sufficiency) ΓÇö direct **procollagen and hydroxyproline** amino-acid substrate during high translational drive.
- **L-cystine** ΓÇö 500 mg twice daily ΓÇö primary sulfur donor for **PAPSS2 PAPS sulfation** of aggrecan and CARS2-linked chondrocyte proliferative support.
- **N-acetylglucosamine (NAG)** ΓÇö 500 mg twice daily ΓÇö direct **NAGK salvage substrate** for UDP-GlcNAc and aggrecan glycosaminoglycan chain synthesis.
- **MSM (methylsulfonylmethane)** ΓÇö 1,500 mg/day ΓÇö auxiliary **inorganic sulfate donor** supporting aggrecan fixed-charge density and Donnan osmotic hydration alongside **L-cystine** and **NAC**.
- **Creatine monohydrate** ΓÇö 3,000ΓÇô5,000 mg/day ΓÇö **CK-B phosphocreatine ATP buffer** sustaining ion pumps, vesicular secretion, and osmoregulatory volume expansion.
- **Potassium citrate** ΓÇö 10 mEq twice daily ΓÇö conditional on improved net **urinary calcium-phosphate supersaturation** and serum potassium headroom.
- **TUDCA** ΓÇö 250 mg twice daily ΓÇö **ER chemical chaperone** that prevents procollagen misfolding and PERK/eIF2alpha ER-stress deceleration (distinct from the **ambroxol/oleate** lipid-recycling branch).
- **N-acetylcysteine (NAC)** ΓÇö 300 mg/day ΓÇö supports intracellular **glutathione synthesis** and sulfate supply during Stage 1 matrix build.

## **V. Stage 2A ΓÇö Lower Load Alignment (Days 7ΓÇô8)**

- **Hydrolyzed collagen peptides** ΓÇö 5,000 mg/day ΓÇö supplies **Gly-Pro-Hyp tripeptides** for collagen fibril maturation and osteoid synthesis across Stage 2.
- **L-citrulline** ΓÇö 3,000 mg/day ΓÇö sustained **eNOS nitric oxide** precursor that supports metaphyseal perfusion and cGMP-mediated actomyosin relaxation alongside **cilostazol**.
- **Potassium citrate (Stage 2A)** ΓÇö 10 mEq twice daily ΓÇö maintains **citrate crystal-restraint** and urinary chemistry balance across Stage 2A.
- **Vitamin K2 (MK-4)** ΓÇö 15 mg three times daily ΓÇö high-tissue-penetration **GGCX cofactor** that carboxylates local **MGP** and osteocalcin to keep mineral restricted to the metaphyseal front.
- **LMHF vibration (lower load)** ΓÇö 35 Hz, 0.15ΓÇô0.20 g, two 10-minute sessions/day separated by 6ΓÇô8 hours ΓÇö **ciliary and cytoskeletal mechanotransduction** stimulus for axial column alignment.

## **VI. Stage 2B ΓÇö Higher Load Conversion (Days 9ΓÇô14)**

- **Dietary calcium** ΓÇö 1,000 mg/day total elemental intake (food counts) ΓÇö supplies **mineral substrate** during Stage 2B osteogenic realization once **MGP** is carboxylated.
- **Hydrolyzed collagen peptides (Stage 2B)** ΓÇö 5,000 mg/day ΓÇö continues **collagen tripeptide** supply for primary spongiosa trabecular formation.
- **L-citrulline (Stage 2B)** ΓÇö 3,000 mg/day ΓÇö maintains **endothelial NO perfusion** at the chondro-osseous replacement front.
- **Potassium citrate (Stage 2B)** ΓÇö 10 mEq twice daily (paired with conditional **magnesium** according to Mg/CPP state) ΓÇö regulates mineral phase and urinary calcium-phosphate supersaturation.
- **Vitamin K2 (MK-4) (Stage 2B)** ΓÇö 15 mg three times daily ΓÇö directs Stage 2B calcium deposition into **metaphyseal spongiosa** while restraining premature physeal bridging.
- **LMHF vibration (higher load)** ΓÇö 35 Hz, 0.25 g, two 10-minute sessions/day separated by 6ΓÇô8 hours ΓÇö stepped-up **mechanotransductive osteogenic loading** for terminal trabecular conversion.

## **VII. Refinements and Frontier Options (State- and Verification-Gated)**

- **Z-endoxifen** ΓÇö 1 mg up to max 2 mg/day ΓÇö CYP2D6-independent **SERM substitute for anastrozole** when peripheral estrogen-receptor modulation is selected instead of aromatase inhibition (never stacked with an AI).
- **rhPAPP-A2** ΓÇö conditional ΓÇö cleaves pericellular **IGFBP-3 and IGFBP-5** inside the cartilage matrix to liberate sequestered local **free IGF-1** right at the chondrocyte surface.

- **G-1** ΓÇö research probe ΓÇö selective **GPER-1 agonism** targeting resting-zone proliferation without activating nuclear **ER-alpha** senescence.
- **Naltriben (or Osteocrin)** ΓÇö research probes ΓÇö downstream **TRPM7/CaMKII volume-execution** probe (bounded by delta-opioid off-target selectivity) or **NPR3 clearance-receptor decoy** preserving local CNP.

- **(+)-Epicatechin** ΓÇö 100 mg twice daily ΓÇö supports **primary-cilia order**, endothelial eNOS, and mitochondrial coupling alongside **SS-31**.
- **Taurine and L-serine** ΓÇö 1,000 mg twice daily taurine + 2,000 mg/day L-serine ΓÇö drives **5-taurinomethyluridine (╧äm5U) mitochondrial tRNA decoding** and SHMT2 one-carbon supply for respiratory subunit translation (stagger taurine ΓëÑ4 hours from morning GAA/creatine).
